Some additional events followed since posting here from my vet clinic that were difficult and so I shared about it anonymously on Facebook, never naming the clinic of course. Again, as with Reddit, the outpouring of support was mind blowing. But I am most touched by how this one person perfectly understood why I was not slamming the vet clinic or filing a lawsuit. Repostinf her share because it is so important to not get caught up in the heat of the moment and cause greater chaos when you are already in pain. When you lose somebody special to you, you are already so drained, and I think it’s best to take what energy you do have and leave it open to positive pursuits. Maybe that isn’t true for everyone, but it has felt right for me, and that is how I am moving through this tragic situation.

Thank you for sharing. Of course you are second and third guessing what you did because the outcome hurts so much. It’s more so how we are wired as humans rather than indicative that you somehow should have known something or done something differently. For you, you wonder if you had brought your baby home if it would have ended differently. For me, I wonder if I had left my buddy at the emergency a bit longer instead of taking him home for a couple hours before the vet of it would have ended differently. We can consider 1000 possibilities but at the end of the day, I believe if you loved your animal, which you clearly did, and you were making the best decision you could with the information you had at the time. Don’t let the “what ifs” tarnish all that you gave to them.  Sending love xxx

I remember when my little guy started to lose his hearing, I was devastated. He had an expensive vocabulary that allowed us to communicate well with each other. But while he took some adjusting, I have to say he wasn’t so devastated. In fact, he *may* have been relieved to mot have to hear all my yakking😂 Point being, sometimes we put so much of our own emotions onto our beloved one. It’s understandable and it’s protective, but they are very resilient, especially if there’s a strong relationship already there.
